label: input token e at original positions 0-3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is e at one of the first four original-phase steps (t = 0..3). Every such step is active (dev precision 1.0) and these steps account for essentially all of the activation mass. The feature does not fire on any other token, on e at original positions 4 and later, at the delimiter, or (apart from about 0.2% of activations, all tiny ~0.02-0.14 of max) on e fed back during the copy phase. Magnitude falls with position: t=0-1 near max (~1.0), t=2 ~0.8, t=3 ~0.35-0.4 of max. Activation is weaker when e has already appeared earlier (in_first=0 steps are mostly the weak cases, e.g. a second e at t=3).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.998, F1 0.999, mass recall 0.9999, with 0 false positives.

All 132 missed activations on the test split are fed-back e in the copy phase. They are tiny (0.02-0.11 of max) and hold 0.0% of the mass. That matches the claim of 'rare and tiny' copy-phase activations, about 0.2% of the total. The profile shows every activation is on in_tok e: no other token fires, and nothing fires at the delimiter.

The magnitude claim fits the dev profile. Active counts are about the same at each t (~16.5k), and mass shares are t0 .298, t1 .316, t2 .266, t3 .120. Taking t=1 as 1.0, that gives t0 about 0.94, t2 about 0.84 and t3 about 0.38, which matches the stated ~0.8 at t=2 and 0.35-0.4 at t=3.

The claim that a repeated e is weaker cannot be tested. Adding n_seen(['e'])>0 to the predicate predicts 0 steps, so e never appears twice within the first 4 original positions in this data (tokens look like they are drawn without repetition there). The explanation already says this claim is unchecked. It is a minor caveat, not an error.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
